# swarmops git export

Send the store's history to git: every commit of --ref's history that the last export into --branch does not reach is written into the git repository at PATH, parents first, made durable, and --branch moves to the export of --ref's head, created if it does not exist.

The repository is written on this host, at PATH, relative to the working directory: a bare repository (git init --bare makes one), or a work tree, which holds .git and whose checked-out branch is refused (E\_INVALID\_ARG). A changeset imported from git exports to the commit it came from, byte for byte; one made in the store exports to a commit with its own signatures and SwarmOps-\* trailers, the same commit every time. Run again, it writes only what the branch does not reach, and nothing when the branch is at the export of --ref's head. It needs no identity.

A branch at a commit that is no export of --ref's head or of an ancestor of it fails with E\_GIT\_EXPORT\_DIVERGED (exit 3), details.reason saying why, and nothing is written; --force moves it all the same, still by compare-and-swap. Then git push sends the branch on.

```yaml
title: "swarmops git export"
description: "Send the store's history to git: write every commit of --ref's history that --branch's last export does not reach into the git repository at PATH, then move --branch to it."
group: "git"
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: false
identity_required: false
mcp_tool: ""
envelope_op: "git_export"
exit_codes: [0, 1, 3]
errors: [E_GIT_EXPORT_DIVERGED, E_GIT_WRITE]
syntax: "swarmops git export [OPTIONS] <PATH>"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops git export [OPTIONS] <PATH>
```

## Required arguments

### `PATH`

Syntax: `<PATH>`.

The git repository's directory.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--ref`

Syntax: `--ref <REF>`.
Default: `main`.

The store ref whose history to export: main or release/&lt;name&gt;.

### `--branch`

Syntax: `--branch <BRANCH>`.
Default: `main`.

The git branch to write, refs/heads/&lt;BRANCH&gt;: main, or a trunk named otherwise, such as stable.

### `--force`

Syntax: `--force`.

Move a branch that diverged all the same, replacing what git holds there (by compare-and-swap; never a checked-out branch).

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
swarmops --repo [tmp]/store git export [git]
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "op": "git_export",
  "api": 1,
  "result": {
    "exported": 1,
    "objects_written": 3,
    "head_changeset": "[c1]",
    "head_sha": "[id2]",
    "branch": "main",
    "branch_moved": true,
    "incremental": false,
    "rewritten": 0
  },
  "meta": {
    "repo": "[tmp]/store",
    "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
    "resolved": {
      "main": "[c1]"
    },
    "auth": "trust"
  }
}
```

Exit code 0. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

## Return information

`result` is a `GitExportResp` (`swarmops schema GitExportResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branch` | `string` | yes | The branch the export wrote, by its short name. |
| `branch_moved` | `boolean` | yes | Whether this export moved the branch, or created it; `false` when the branch named `head_sha` already, after an earlier export of the same head or a concurrent one. |
| `exported` | `integer` | yes | How many commits this export wrote to the repository: the commits of the ref's history that the branch's last export did not reach and the repository did not hold. A branch that is up to date exports 0. |
| `head_changeset` | `string` | yes | The changeset at `source_ref`'s head, which `head_sha` is the export of. |
| `head_sha` | `string` | yes | The commit the branch names now, the export of `head_changeset`: its git id, 40 lowercase hex digits. |
| `incremental` | `boolean` | yes | Whether the branch held an earlier export that this one continued, so that only the commits after it were written; `false` for a branch the export created, or one that `force` moved from a history that was no export of this one. |
| `objects_written` | `integer` | yes | How many git objects (commits, trees and blobs) this export wrote to the repository. |
| `old_sha` | `string or null` | no | The commit the branch named when the export started; omitted when the branch did not exist, and the export created it. |
| `rewritten` | `integer` | yes | How many of the exported commits have another id than the commit they were imported from: a commit the import took lossily (`git.lossy`) renders to other bytes than the git commit it came from, and so does every commit above it, whose parent has another id now; their signature headers no longer verify. Commits made in the store were never imported and are not counted. |
| `warnings` | `array of string` | no | What the export has to say that did not stop it, such as how many of its commits it rewrote (`rewritten`). Omitted when empty. |

Envelope `op`: `git_export`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.
- `3`: The change conflicts with what it lands on: resolve it, then run the operation again.

## Errors

- [`E_GIT_EXPORT_DIVERGED`](../errors.md#e_git_export_diverged) (exit 3): `git export`: the branch holds commits that are not the export of the source ref's head or of an ancestor of it, so the branch did not move; there is no silent merge, and the request's `force` moves it anyway.
- [`E_GIT_WRITE`](../errors.md#e_git_write) (exit 1): `git export` could not write the repository; `details.reason` says what failed: `io` (the filesystem refused a write; `details.path` names the file, relative to the git directory), `ref_locked` (the branch's lock file, `refs/heads/<branch>.lock`, exists: another git process holds it, or an earlier export died holding it, and git itself says to remove it once no git process runs; `details.path` names it) or `ref_name_conflict` (an existing ref stands where the branch's name needs a directory, or the other way round; `details.branch`).

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
